London, 16<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Toyota Motor Corp** . said it would further cut production at several North American plants over the next few months in an effort to reduce vehicle inventories by half. Its latest move sets non-production days at manufacturing facilities in Canada and in Kentucky, California, Texas, Indiana, West Virginia and Alabama. The disclosure dims prospects that production cuts already made by Toyota and other automakers will be enough to make up for the weakest demand for autos in decades. General Motors said yesterday it’s bracing for industrywide sales in the United States to fall to 10.5 million in 2009, a 27-year low. And Chrysler LLC said it would keep some plants closed beyond a one-month shutdown that was scheduled to end this week. The two U.S. automakers are using $4 billion federal loans to avoid collapse.  Toyota declined to disclose the actual number of vehicles involved in the planned output cut.  Toyota said last week it would halt production at its Japanese plants for 11 days in February and March.  It had already reduced North American production of its best-selling cars, including the Camry and Corolla sedans, and suspended work on a new plant in Mississippi that was due to start producing the popular Prius gasolineelectric hybrid car from 2010. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Chrysler LLC** will extend shutdowns at five factories one week beyond the scheduled reopening date of Monday, Jan. 19.  Assembly plants in Belvidere, Ill.; Sterling Heights, Mich.; and Toluca, Mexico, will reopen Jan. 26, the company said today. Chrysler’s Global Engine Manufacturing Alliance engine joint venture and its Trenton, Mich., engine plant also will take an extra week and reopen Jan. 26. Chrysler attributed the extended shutdown to difficult economic conditions.  Chrysler says it will reopen assembly plants in Windsor, Ontario (minivan), and Conner Avenue in Detroit (Viper) on Feb. 2, the same date as announced in December. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Sales of new cars in Europe** declined 8 percent last year, as consumer sentiment turned sour particularly in the second half, the German automotive industry association VDA said on Wednesday. The region’s dealerships sold 14.7 million vehicles, including 13.6 million in Western Europe, VDA said. “The situation has worsened dramatically in the second half,” the group said, citing a drop in consumer confidence amid the financial crisis and banks’ reticence to make loans to prospective buyers.  While unit sales were down 3 percent year-on-year in Western Europe in the first half, the decline was 15 percent in the second.  New-car sales in the EU’s new member states Poland, Czech Republic, Romania and Hungary declined about 1 percent to 1.2 million cars last year, VDA’s report showed. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Eskom** expects no growth in the country’s power demand for the next two years as the global economic crisis curbs appetite f

or commodity exports.  “For the next two years we expect no growth in energy requirements,” Brian Dames, the head of state-owned Eskom’s power generation unit, said. “None of us really know what is happening” with the economic downturn.  It may ease pressure on Eskom to raise funding for a five-year, 353 billion rand ($35 billion) expansion to ease an electricity shortage that’s curbing economic growth in Africa’s biggest economy. South Africa’s power demand rose by 4.3 percent in 2007, according to government figures.  Eskom is forecasting that demand growth will resume at a rate of 2 percent to 3 percent a year after the next two years, Dames said. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Northam Platinum** has announced that the planned rebuild of the smelter was completed on schedule and within budget and the smelter was re-commissioned during December 2008. _Source: Northam Platinum_
